summary: Takayoshi Kamei was a history, archaeology, and Japanology scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (c. 1908–1912). He later held posts at the University of Tokyo (c. 1930–1947), Ibaraki University (c. 1950–1959), and Seisen University (c. 1959–1969).

Takayoshi Namikawa is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who completed multiple degrees at Bukkyo University between c. 1969 and 1996. He served as professor at Bukkyo University from 1981 and became professor emeritus in 2018.

Takayuki Hirosawa is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen. His career includes posts at Taisho University, where he was a group member until 1991 and attested as professor in 2014.

Takehiro Sueki was a philosopher who studied at the University of Tokyo from c. 1941 to 1944. He held academic posts at the University of Electro-Communications (c. 1951–1968), the University of Tokyo (c. 1968–1982), and Toyo University (c. 1982–1992).

Takeo Hibino was a history, archaeology, and Sinology scholar who studied at Kyoto University (c. 1933–1936). He worked at the Academy of Oriental Culture, Kyoto Institute, Kyoto University (1948–1977), Otemon Gakuin University (1977), and Otemae University (1980).
Takeo Izumi is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Tohoku University from c. 1973 to 1977 and later served there as a professor from c. 2002 to 2018.

Takeo Kanaseki was a history and archaeology scholar who studied at Kyoto University from c. 1919 to 1923. He later held posts at Kyushu University (c. 1950–1960), Tottori University (c. 1960–1969), and Tezukayama Gakuin University (c. 1969–1979).

Takeo Kuwabara was a philosopher who studied at Kyoto University (c. 1925–1928). He held academic posts at Tohoku University from c. 1934 to 1949 and served as a professor at Kyoto University from c. 1949 to 1968.

Takeshi Fujii is a historian and Indologist who studied at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies and the University of Delhi. He spent his academic career at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies, becoming professor in 2001 and professor emeritus in 2021.

Takeshi Hasegawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He held a post at Ryukoku University (attested 1998) and lecturer posts at both the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

Takeshi Karashima was a Sinology scholar who studied at Tokyo Imperial University (c. 1923–1927). His career included posts at Keijo Imperial University (c. 1930–1945), Sagami Women's University, Showa Women's University, and Kamakura's library.

Takeshi Umehara was a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied at Nagoya and Kyoto universities, and held posts at Ritsumeikan University (1955–1970), Kyoto City University of Arts (1972–1986), and the International Research Center for Japanese Studies (1987–1995).

Takeshiro Kuraishi was a Sinology and linguistics scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (c. 1925–1928). He served as a professor at Kyoto University (c. 1939–1949) and held a post at the University of Tokyo (c. 1950–1958).

Takezo Kaneko was a philosopher who studied at the University of Tokyo (c. 1926–1929) under Tetsuro Watsuji. He held posts at Hokkaido University, the University of Tokyo (professor c. 1948–1966), Seikei University (c. 1966–1971), and International Christian University (c. 1971–1976).
Taklung Tsetrul Rinpoche was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Po Lu Khenpo Dorjé. He succeeded Trulshik Rinpoche in 2012 and taught Phakchok Rinpoche.

Taku Fukuda is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Hajime Sakurabe. He was appointed lecturer at Doho University in 1995 and is attested in 2026 as a Doho University professor and Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute affiliate.

Takudo Ishikawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He held a researcher post at Jodo Shu Research Institute (attested 2005) and teaching posts at Taisho University (attested 2015 and 2026).

Takushu Sugimoto is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who earned his degrees at Tohoku University. He served as professor at Kanazawa University (c. 1985–1999; emeritus c. 1999), Komazawa University (attested 1990), and Kinjo University (c. 2000).

Tampalawela Dhammaratana is a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the University of Kelaniya, University of Paris under Jean-François Lyotard, Paris-Sorbonne University under Michel Hulin, and École Pratique des Hautes Études under Pierre-Sylvain Filliozat.

Tan Chung was a scholar of Sinology and history/archaeology who earned his PhD from Visva-Bharati University. He served as Professor of Chinese at the University of Delhi (c. 1968–1978) and department head at Jawaharlal Nehru University (c. 1978–1994).
